summary: In Greek mythology, Coeranus (Ancient Greek Κοίρανος) is a Lycian warrior in Sarpedon's host whom Odysseus slays when Athena turns him against the Lycians. Handbook tradition sometimes names him son of Iphitus; he is distinct from Coeranus the Cretan charioteer of Meriones.

sections.heading: Lycian slain by Odysseus
paragraphs: Homer (Iliad 5.677–678) lists Coeranus among the Lycians Odysseus kills when Athena turns his mind from Hector to the Lycian mass. Wikipedia's Coeranus (mythology) page records him as a Lycian soldier, son of Iphitus, following Sarpedon — separate from the Lyctian charioteer Hector kills at the ships (Iliad 17).
Ovid (Metamorphoses 13.257) has Odysseus boast of the same kill in his contest for Achilles' arms.

sections.heading: Homonym care
paragraphs: The atlas id coeranus-lycian is the Iliadic Lycian alone — not coeranus-lyctian, nor the Argive Melampodid Coerani on the same Wikipedia page.
